subject: Anthropology
title: Archaeology
description: A micro-lesson that makes Archaeology usable.

hook.text: A broken pot in the desert tells a story: who made it, what they ate, how they traded, and when they vanished.

buildup.text: Archaeology studies past human life through material remains — tools, buildings, trash, and landscapes.

discovery.text: It reconstructs entire civilizations from fragments. A seed reveals diet; a road reveals a trade empire.

twist.text: Archaeology gives voice to people who left no written records — the vast majority of human history.

climax.text: Without archaeology, 99% of human history would be silent. Objects speak when documents don't exist.

punchline.text: The past survives in what people left behind.

quiz.question: Why is archaeology important for understanding human history?
options: It recovers history from material remains when no texts exist

details.summary: Archaeology studies past human societies through their material remains — tools, buildings, pottery, food residues, and landscapes. It extends human history far beyond written records, revealing how people lived for the vast majority of our species' 300,000-year existence.
details.whyItMatters: Archaeology is the only way to study human societies before writing was invented. Without it, 95% of human history would be completely unknown. It reveals long-term patterns of cultural change invisible to methods limited to recent centuries.
takeaways: Archaeology studies the past through material remains and sites
It reveals human history far beyond the reach of written records
It is essential for understanding 95% of the human past

faq.question: How is archaeology related to anthropology?
faq.answer: In the American tradition, archaeology is a subfield of anthropology, sharing its holistic and comparative perspective. Archaeologists interpret material remains using anthropological theories about culture, social organization, and adaptation. In Europe, archaeology is often a separate discipline.

faq.question: Is archaeology just about digging things up?
faq.answer: Excavation is only one part. Modern archaeology involves remote sensing, geochemical analysis, computer modeling, environmental reconstruction, and ethnographic analogy. Much archaeological research uses material already excavated.
